concept_options.title: The ruler where 1 is six times wider than 9
concept_options.hook: Nine digits, and the ruler they live on was never evenly marked.
concept_options.visual_approach: A logarithmic ruler built in Manim as a physical object — bone-white rules on a slate ground, unequal tick spacing, a vernier caliper that opens across a stretch and reports its width. The nine stretches are measured, then the ruler performs one continuous transformation: it stands up and becomes the familiar Benford bar chart. Every frame is drawn geometry; nothing is photographed and nothing is a stock chart component. A Remotion layer sits on top of the Manim footage carrying the section chip, the burned captions and the annotation callouts.
concept_options.target_audience: General audience on a phone. No mathematics assumed; the word 'logarithm' is never spoken.
key_points: Nine possible leading digits, so eleven percent each is the obvious guess
The real answer is 30.1% for 1 and 4.6% for 9
The cause is spacing, not statistics: growth is multiplicative, so the number line that matters is the one where 1 to 2 is the same move as 10 to 20
On that ruler the stretch labelled 1 is 0.301 of the length and the stretch labelled 9 is 0.046 — six and a half times smaller
Cut the nine stretches out, stand them up, and you have built the distribution
Auditors use the mismatch: hand-invented figures come out too even, because even is what a person reaches for when trying to look random
The precondition — data spanning orders of magnitude — is also the limit: point the ruler at bounded data and it can say nothing
concept_options.core_message: The bias in leading digits is not a statistical curiosity, it is the visible width of an interval; and the same width that makes the test work is what makes most public uses of it invalid.
concept_options.tone: Precise, unhurried, faintly forensic. The tone of someone showing you a measurement rather than telling you a fact.
grounded_in: underserved_gap: the log ruler as a measurable object, drawn rather than named
underserved_gap: fusing the power and the limit into one sentence
data_point: log10(1+1/d) is the width of [log d, log d+1]
data_point: precinct counts and adult heights fail the precondition
audience pain point: every explanation loses the reader at 'uniformly distributed on a logarithmic scale'
concept_options.why_this_works: It closes the exact gap the research found. The canonical treatments state the reason in words and then show the bar chart as a separate object, leaving the viewer to accept the link on faith. Here the link is a single continuous move that the viewer watches happen, so the chart is not presented as evidence — it is assembled in front of them out of the thing that caused it. It is also the only concept whose central image is impossible to photograph and awkward in every runtime except a mathematical-animation engine, which is the world the style ledger requires next.

concept_options.title: Fake numbers are too fair
concept_options.hook: Sit down and invent a hundred figures. You will give yourself away in the first digit.
concept_options.visual_approach: Open inside the act of fabrication: a column of invented figures accumulating, their leading digits tallied beside them into nine near-equal stacks. Then the real distribution drops in over the top and refuses to match. The law is never named until the last five seconds.
concept_options.target_audience: General audience; skews toward the true-crime and 'how they got caught' appetite
key_points: A person inventing numbers spreads leading digits roughly evenly
Even is what feels random and real data is never even
Nearly half of real leading digits are 1 or 2
Digit analysis is a screen that tells an auditor where to look
concept_options.core_message: The tell is not that the fake numbers are wrong, it is that they are too fair.
grounded_in: data_point: fabricated statements usually do not conform
data_point: nearly half of real leading digits are 1 or 2
concept_options.why_this_works: The strongest hook of the four, because it puts the viewer in the seat of the person being caught rather than the person doing the catching. Its weakness is that it can only assert why the real distribution is uneven — the actual mechanism does not fit inside the story, so the video ends up asking for trust at exactly the moment the ruler concept earns it.

concept_options.title: Read from the dirt on the page
concept_options.hook: In 1881 a man worked out a law of nature by noticing which pages of a book were dirty.
concept_options.visual_approach: The fore-edge of a closed book of logarithm tables, the dirt graded across it; the grading is itself the distribution. Then Benford in 1938 with twenty unrelated datasets converging on the same curve, and the modern forensic use as the final beat.
concept_options.target_audience: General audience with an appetite for history-of-science
key_points: Newcomb, 1881: the early pages of shared logarithm tables were more worn
Benford, 1938: over 20,000 numbers from 20 unrelated datasets
River lengths, physical constants, street addresses, baseball statistics — all the same curve
The same curve is now a forensic screen
concept_options.core_message: A distribution was read off the grease on a book before anyone could explain it.
concept_options.why_this_works: Genuinely charming and completely true. It is also the single most saturated opening in the entire corpus — the research found it leading nearly every article on the subject — and a timeline spends its running time on chronology rather than on mechanism. Kept as one line inside the selected concept rather than as its spine.

concept_options.title: Three datasets, one test, one result you should not trust
concept_options.hook: Same test, three datasets. It is only telling the truth about two of them.
concept_options.visual_approach: Three panels running the same digit test in parallel — a set of invoices, a set of adult heights, a set of precinct vote counts — with the expected curve overlaid on each. Two deviate. Only one of the deviations means anything.
concept_options.target_audience: Numerate general audience; people who have seen the law invoked online
key_points: The test is a comparison against a fixed curve
Bounded data deviates for reasons that have nothing to do with honesty
Adult heights are almost all between 1 and 2 metres
Precinct counts do not span orders of magnitude, so researchers reject Benford tests as election evidence
concept_options.core_message: A failed test is not a finding until you have checked that the test applied.
grounded_in: data_point: the precondition is data spanning orders of magnitude
expert: Golbeck — useful for many things, invalidating an election is not one
misconception: a failed test proves fabrication
concept_options.why_this_works: The most publicly useful of the four and the most defensible. But it is a correction, and a correction has to assume the thing it corrects — in fifty vertical seconds it would spend its whole budget establishing a law it then spends no time explaining. Its payload is folded into the last twelve seconds of the selected concept instead, where it lands as a turn rather than a lecture.

selected_concept.rationale: It is the only concept that both closes the gap the research identified and satisfies the style ledger. The gap: every existing treatment says 'uniformly distributed on a logarithmic scale' and then shows the nine descending bars, with the connection left to trust — here the bars are physically assembled out of the ruler that caused them, in one continuous move, and no formula is ever spoken. The ledger: the two prior productions were both hand-authored Remotion vector compositions, and the manifesto requires a different drawn world; this concept's central image is a measured geometric transformation, which is Manim's native subject and nobody else's. Concept c-threewindows contributed its payload to the final twelve seconds, and c-dirtybook contributed one line.
modifications: Absorb the precondition argument from c-threewindows as the closing turn, so the video ends on a limit rather than on a capability
Absorb one line from c-dirtybook — the worn pages — as a single aside rather than an opening beat, because the research marks that opening as saturated
Drop the formula log10(1 + 1/d) from the narration entirely; it appears once, small, as a measured caption on the ruler, where it is a label on something visible rather than an explanation

tools.role: Every moving image in the video. Manim CE 0.21.0 renders the ruler, the caliper, the stretch measurement, the stand-up transformation, the fabricated ledger and the two span windows as separate 1080x1920 clips.
tools.why_this_provider: The world required by the style ledger, and the only local engine whose native object is a measured geometric transformation. Runs offline; no key, no network.

tools.role: English narration, synthesised per script section so each section's true duration is measured rather than estimated
tools.why_this_provider: The only TTS configured on this machine. The en_US-ryan-high voice was fetched from the rhasspy/piper GitHub release because the HuggingFace voice host is blocked by the environment's network policy.

stages.approach: Author the Manim scenes by hand as one Python module per beat, rendered at 1080x1920 30fps to projects/<id>/assets/video/. Read .agents/skills/manimce-best-practices before writing any scene. Narration is synthesised first so the animation timings are cut to real measured audio, not the other way round.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: None accepted. Manim is the approved world; substituting a different runtime would be a silent world swap and is forbidden by the manifesto's rotation rule.

tools.role: Hand-authored Remotion composition in atelier mode: the Manim clips are the footage bed, and the Remotion layer carries the section chip, the burned captions, the annotation callouts and the closing card.
tools.why_this_provider: Remotion is the only runtime here that can composite typography over an existing video track with frame-exact caption timing. It supplies the glass, not the image.

stages.approach: composition_mode: atelier. Manim clips are mounted with OffthreadVideo from absolute paths; every typographic element is written for this piece. No stock scene types, no reusable components — the atelier import scan enforces this.
stages.fallback_if_unavailable: ffmpeg burn-in of an SRT, which would lose the chip and the annotations. Escalate before accepting.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Piper is a small local neural voice. It is intelligible and correctly stressed but has a narrower dynamic range than a cloud voice, and it is the weakest component of all three productions so far.
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Ship on Piper. A cloud TTS key would be the single largest quality upgrade available to this channel, but the standing constraint is that nothing is paid for until the channel earns.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Manim's default look — dark navy ground, thin smooth vector strokes, its bundled typeface — is instantly recognisable and would make this read as a generic maths channel.
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Override every default: slate ground, bone-white heavy rules, Space Grotesk and Space Mono installed to the system font path, mechanical stepped motion instead of Manim's default smooth easing. The engine is used for its geometry, never for its taste.

quality_tradeoffs.tradeoff: Compositing two runtimes doubles the render surface and adds a class of failure — path handling, colour, frame alignment — that a single-runtime piece does not have.
quality_tradeoffs.recommendation: Accept it. It is the architecture that makes the manifesto concrete: the reference video's grammar of annotation-over-footage, with drawn footage underneath. Render Manim first, review stills, then composite.

alternative_paths.description: Manim only — burn the captions and the chip inside Manim and skip Remotion entirely.
alternative_paths.what_changes: One runtime, simpler pipeline. But caption timing becomes hand-placed inside animation code, the section chip cannot persist cleanly across clip boundaries, and the annotation layer loses the reference's grammar. Rejected.

alternative_paths.description: Remotion atelier only — draw the ruler in SVG by hand as in the two previous productions.
alternative_paths.what_changes: A third consecutive Remotion vector piece. Violates the manifesto's world-rotation rule and the style ledger's motion-character field. Rejected on identity grounds, not capability grounds.

alternative_paths.description: The same edit with a cloud TTS voice in place of Piper.
alternative_paths.what_changes: Materially better narration — the one upgrade that would lift all three videos. Blocked by the standing 'nothing paid' constraint; recorded so the option stays visible.

production_plan.art_direction: Design read: a machine shop for numbers. The frame is a slate work surface on which a measuring instrument is laid out and read. Ground is deep slate-navy #161A26 — deliberately neither the near-black of the oscilloscope piece nor the warm paper of the plate piece. All structure and all language are bone #F0EAD8, drawn as heavy matte rules rather than thin glowing traces. One accent, chartreuse #C9E265, marks whatever is actually true: the measured widths, the real distribution. One reserved colour, magenta #E5487B, appears exactly once, at the turn, on the beat where the law is pointed at data it cannot judge. Fabricated data is drawn as hollow bone outline — empty, not coloured — so the real/fake contrast costs no additional hue. Signature device: a vernier caliper, drawn as a physical object with jaws, which opens across a stretch of the ruler and reports its width; it returns in the last beat measuring the span of a dataset instead of a digit, which is how the power and the limit become the same gesture. Motion character: mechanical stepping. The caliper snaps between fixed positions, bars rise in quantised jumps, nothing eases in or out and nothing overshoots — with one exception, the single continuous move where the ruler stands up and becomes the chart, which is the centrepiece precisely because it is the only smooth thing in the piece. Type: Space Grotesk 700 for language, Space Mono 400 for every measured number; neither family has been used before here. Layout set: a 3x3 grid of hollow boxes, a horizontal ruler in the middle third with the caliper above it, a shaded stretch column, the standing-up transformation across the lower two thirds, a top-anchored ledger of invented figures, two stacked span windows, and a closing frame with the caliper left open. The test at the end: could this be any other video's frame — no, the whole piece is one instrument being read; does it reuse a look made before — no, neither previous production has a grid, a caliper, a slate ground, stepped motion, or these two typefaces.

taste_profile.design_read: A machine shop for numbers: an instrument laid on a slate bench and read aloud.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: grammar only, from productions/references/wpmavi-power-lines: a persistent chip naming the current idea, burned captions with the load-bearing word marked, annotation drawn onto what you are looking at, one accent plus one reserved colour used exactly once, cuts every four to five seconds. None of the reference's clothes — not its pill shape, not its yellow, not its typeface.
anti_patterns: Manim's factory defaults in any form — its ground colour, its stroke weight, its bundled typeface, its smooth default easing
The nine descending bars presented as the argument rather than assembled as its result
The worn-logarithm-tables origin as an opening beat
Any glow, bloom or scanline — that is the oscilloscope piece
Any paper grain, plate border or ink texture — that is the tides piece
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Four values, no more. Slate ground #161A26, bone #F0EAD8 for all structure and all language, chartreuse #C9E265 as the single accent marking whatever is measurably true, magenta #E5487B held in reserve for exactly one appearance at the turn. Fabricated data is drawn as hollow bone outline rather than given a hue, so the real/fake contrast costs nothing from the budget.
taste_profile.layout_variation: A different disposition of the frame in every beat: a 3x3 grid of hollow boxes; a horizontal ruler in the middle third with the caliper above it; a shaded stretch column; the standing-up transformation across the lower two thirds; a top-anchored ledger of invented figures; two stacked span windows; a closing frame with the caliper left open. No hero element repeated beat to beat with new text underneath — that is the scene-level templating trap.
quality_gates: Every tick position computed from log10; the nine reported widths sum to 1.000
No Manim default survives: not its ground colour, not its stroke weight, not its bundled typeface, not its easing
Exactly one continuous move in the whole piece; everything else steps or runs at a machined constant rate
Magenta appears once and only once
Reviewed against both STYLE_LEDGER.md rows on all five fields before render

music_source.mood_direction: Silence under the narration, with one self-produced element: a low machined tick that runs only while the caliper is on screen and stops the moment the ruler begins to stand up. Produced locally with ffmpeg synthesis; no library, no provider, no key.

voice_selection.rationale: The only TTS available offline on this machine. Measured at 3.3 words per second on the two prior productions, which is the basis for the timing plan.
voice_selection.delivery_style: Level and unhurried, with the pauses carried by the edit rather than by the voice. The forensic tone comes from the pacing of the images, not from performance.
voice_selection.pacing_policy: Synthesise per script section, measure the real duration of each, and cut the animation to those measurements. Never estimate.

line_items.operation: Manim CE local render, seven scenes at 1080x1920 30fps
Narration synthesis, one wav per script section
line_items.notes: Local neural TTS, voice fetched from a GitHub release
Local Node render using the Playwright Chromium already symlinked into remotion-composer

line_items.operation: Audio mux, loudness normalisation to -14 LUFS, faststart

savings_options: Already at zero. The only paid option anywhere in this plan is a cloud TTS voice, which is declined under the standing constraint.

approval.user_notes: Standing pre-authorisation from the user, given explicitly and repeatedly across this channel's productions: full decision authority, no questions at any gate, choose the topic and the design. The constraints attached to that authority are: vertical short, original script, natural fluent English narration, burned captions, royalty-free or self-produced audio, and nothing paid for. Recorded here rather than as a decision_log entry because the decision_log schema's category enum does not contain 'approval_policy' even though AGENT_GUIDE.md requires that category for full-run pre-authorisation — the same schema/guide disagreement flagged on the two previous productions.

metadata.world_rotation_check: productions/STYLE_LEDGER.md records Remotion atelier as the world for both prior productions. Manim is unused. The manifesto requires that two consecutive productions not share a world; this satisfies it. Remotion still appears in the plan, but only as the compositing layer over Manim imagery — the drawn world, meaning where every pixel of the image comes from, is Manim.
metadata.ledger_overlap_check: Checked against both existing rows on all five fields. Design read: new (machine shop for numbers; prior rows are an oscilloscope in a dark room and a corrected physics-book page). Ground and palette roles: new (slate #161A26, bone, chartreuse, magenta reserved once; prior grounds were #080B10 and #EDE6D6). Signature device: new (a caliper as a physical object; prior devices were a running microsecond counter and three unequal arrows). Layout set: new. Motion character: new (mechanical stepping with a single continuous exception; prior characters were constant-velocity flight and spring overshoot). One honest warning to record in the ledger: the caliper is adjacent to the engineering dimension line used once in the oscilloscope piece. They are drawn as different objects — a caliper has jaws and a body and is present as a tool, a dimension line is an annotation — and the overlap is on part of one field of five, which the ledger's own rule treats as a warning rather than a re-design.
metadata.decision_log_schema_note: AGENT_GUIDE.md requires full-run pre-authorisation to be recorded as a decision_log entry with category 'approval_policy', but that value is absent from the category enum in schemas/artifacts/decision_log.schema.json. The pre-authorisation is therefore recorded in proposal_packet.approval.user_notes, as on the two previous productions. The disagreement between the guide and the schema is a standing defect worth fixing in one place or the other.

decisions.subject: Pipeline for a fully generated vertical explainer short

options_considered.label: animated-explainer
options_considered.reason: Topic-to-explainer with a research stage, an eight-stage contract and schema-validated artifacts. The subject has no source footage and no presenter.

options_considered.label: animation
options_considered.reason: Motion-graphics-first. Would suit the visual, but drops the research stage that the concept depends on.
options_considered.rejected_because: The whole concept came out of the research stage's landscape scan; a pipeline without one would have produced the saturated angle.

options_considered.label: hybrid
options_considered.reason: Source footage plus support visuals.
options_considered.rejected_because: There is no source footage and, under productions/MANIFESTO.md, there never will be.

decisions.reason: It is the pipeline whose first stage is research, and this concept exists only because the research found that the standard explanation and the standard visual have never been joined.

decisions.subject: Angle and narrative structure for the Benford's Law short

options_considered.label: The ruler where 1 is six times wider than 9
options_considered.reason: Closes the identified gap by assembling the bar chart out of the ruler that causes it, in one continuous move, with no formula spoken. Also the only concept whose central image is native to the drawn world the ledger requires next.

options_considered.label: Fake numbers are too fair
options_considered.reason: The strongest hook of the four and a genuinely underserved framing.
options_considered.rejected_because: The mechanism does not fit inside the story, so the video would have to assert the uneven distribution at exactly the moment the ruler concept can demonstrate it. Its hook survives inside c-ruler's fraud beat.

options_considered.label: Three datasets, one test, one result you should not trust
options_considered.reason: The most publicly useful and the most defensible of the four.
options_considered.rejected_because: A correction has to assume the thing it corrects; in fifty seconds it would spend its whole budget establishing a law it never explains. Its payload was absorbed as c-ruler's closing turn.

options_considered.label: Read from the dirt on the page
options_considered.reason: Charming, true, and the origin of the whole subject.
options_considered.rejected_because: The research marks it as the single most saturated opening in the corpus, and a timeline spends its running time on chronology rather than mechanism. Reduced to one aside.

decisions.reason: It is the only one of the four that shows rather than states, and the only one that ends on a limit rather than a capability. The other three each contributed something: the forger's hook, the precondition turn, and one line of history.

decisions.subject: Drawn world for this production, under the manifesto's rotation rule

options_considered.label: Manim CE 0.21.0 (math_animate)
options_considered.reason: Unused by this channel, and its native subject is exactly this video's central image: a measured geometric transformation carried out continuously in front of the viewer.

options_considered.label: Remotion atelier vector composition
options_considered.reason: Proven twice here and fully understood; would certainly work.
options_considered.rejected_because: It carried both prior productions. productions/MANIFESTO.md forbids two consecutive productions sharing a world, and STYLE_LEDGER.md records the groove that rule exists to break.

options_considered.label: threejs_world
options_considered.reason: Unused, and would satisfy the rotation rule.
options_considered.rejected_because: The argument is one-dimensional — a length along a ruler. Putting it in a 3D world would add dimensions the subject does not have.

options_considered.label: HyperFrames kinetic typography
options_considered.reason: Unused, available, and strong when the words are the visual.
options_considered.rejected_because: Here the words are not the visual; a measured width is. Held for a future production where the type is the subject.

options_considered.label: Ink Theater / Ink Puppet
options_considered.reason: Unused and would rotate the world decisively.
options_considered.rejected_because: A hand-drawn character acting out an interval width would be charming and imprecise, and this piece's entire claim is that you can check the measurement.

decisions.reason: The ledger requires a world that is not Remotion atelier, and of the four unused worlds Manim is the only one whose native object is a measured transformation. Its factory look is explicitly rejected in the art direction — the engine is used for its geometry, never for its taste.

decisions.subject: Composition runtime for the final assembly

options_considered.label: Remotion (available: true)
options_considered.reason: The only runtime here that can mount the Manim clips as a footage bed via OffthreadVideo and lay frame-exact burned captions, a persistent section chip and annotation callouts over them. Chromium is already symlinked into remotion-composer from the Playwright install, so the blocked remotion.media download does not apply.

options_considered.label: HyperFrames (available: true)
options_considered.reason: Available on this machine and excellent at HTML/GSAP kinetic typography.
options_considered.rejected_because: Its strength is generating the visual, and here the visual arrives pre-rendered from Manim. It would be carrying type over video, which is the one job Remotion does better and which this repository already has a caption pipeline for.

options_considered.label: FFmpeg with a burned SRT (available: true)
options_considered.reason: Simplest possible path, always available, and it would concatenate the Manim clips correctly.
options_considered.rejected_because: It cannot carry the persistent section chip or the annotation layer, and an SRT burn discards the per-piece caption styling the manifesto calls for. Retained as the escalation fallback only.

decisions.reason: All three runtimes are available on this machine and all three were evaluated. Remotion is chosen for compositing only — it supplies the glass over the Manim image, not the image. If it became unavailable at compose time that is a blocker to escalate, not a silent swap.

options_considered.reason: Hero work for a channel whose entire stated identity is that nothing is reused. The stock scene-type catalog is off-limits and the atelier path's import scan enforces it.

options_considered.label: Templated — stock cut.type scenes
options_considered.reason: Fast, cheap and reliable.
options_considered.rejected_because: It is the documented reason videos look alike, and this channel exists because five of them did.

decisions.subject: Source of the visual material — drawn versus photographed

options_considered.label: Every frame drawn (Manim), per productions/MANIFESTO.md
options_considered.reason: The channel's stated position. A stock clip is a picture of a subject; this video's subject is an interval width, which has no photograph.

options_considered.label: Pexels or Pixabay footage under the annotation layer
options_considered.reason: Would reproduce the reference video's literal form.
options_considered.rejected_because: Two reasons, and the second is the real one. Mechanically, this environment's network policy denies every media host tested — thirteen of them, recorded in productions/ENVIRONMENT.md. Editorially, the manifesto rejects it regardless: an annotation over a photograph can only point at whatever the photograph happens to contain, and nothing photographable contains 30.1% of a logarithmic ruler.

decisions.reason: The manifesto, and the subject. This topic was chosen partly because it has no photographable object at all.

decisions.subject: Style playbook

options_considered.label: minimalist-diagram
options_considered.reason: Technical deep-dive framing, one idea per frame, structure over decoration. Closest of the five to a measuring instrument being read.

options_considered.label: premium-minimalist
options_considered.reason: Expert-explainer register.
options_considered.rejected_because: Its restraint is a luxury register; this piece's restraint is a workshop register.

options_considered.label: flat-motion-graphics
options_considered.reason: Built for social pacing.
options_considered.rejected_because: Its bounce and colour would undo the mechanical motion character the ledger requires this piece to establish.

decisions.reason: Carried as taste input only. The binding art direction is the taste_profile in the proposal, which overrides the playbook wherever they disagree — the playbook is a starting register, not a look.

decisions.subject: Whether the drawn ruler is dimensionally true

options_considered.label: Tick positions computed from log10, widths reported to three decimals
options_considered.reason: The piece's whole claim is that you can check the measurement. If the stretch labelled 1 is not really 0.301 of the ruler, the argument is a picture of an argument.

options_considered.label: Approximate spacing tuned for legibility
options_considered.reason: Slightly easier to lay out on a narrow frame.
options_considered.rejected_because: The previous production established that the geometry is load-bearing — its arrow lengths came from the real inverse-square pull. Breaking that here would cost more than it saves.

decisions.reason: Every tick position in the Manim scenes is computed as log10(d), and the nine reported widths are log10(1 + 1/d) rounded to three decimals: .301 .176 .125 .097 .079 .067 .058 .051 .046. They sum to 1.000. Nothing is exaggerated for legibility.
